headline: Funding flows. Unicorns multiply. Diplomacy wobbles.
deck: This week sees a mix of funding successes and geopolitical hesitations in space.

stories.head: True Anomaly raises $190M for co-orbital security
stories.body: True Anomaly's $190 million Series C round at a $1.6 billion valuation underscores the increasing demand for co-orbital security solutions. With the DoD's pull-through, this funding reflects a serious commitment to addressing emerging threats in space. Investors are clearly betting that the future of security lies above us.
stories.soWhat: If True Anomaly's growth trajectory continues, it might make the rest of the space security sector look like a slow-moving target.

stories.head: Space unicorns grow, but valuations raise eyebrows
stories.body: SpaceNews has updated its unicorn tracker, revealing an expanding list of private space companies valued over $1 billion. While these valuations suggest a booming sector, the sustainability of such inflated numbers is questionable—especially as the market matures. Investors should be wary of the hype surrounding these figures.
stories.soWhat: The unicorn label may be more about aspiration than reality, and the reckoning could be painful for those caught in the hype.

stories.head: Switzerland opts out of Copernicus funding
stories.body: Switzerland's decision to withdraw from the EU's Copernicus Earth observation program funding cycle has reignited debates about the value of such contributions. The Swiss government appears to prioritize its neutrality over collaborative space initiatives, which could have longer-term implications for European space efforts.
stories.soWhat: If neutrality becomes the norm, collaborative projects may find themselves in a precarious position, relying on a dwindling pool of willing participants.

watchlist.title: Keep an eye on Katalyst Space's demo mission
watchlist.body: With $12 million in funding, Katalyst Space is gearing up for a critical demo mission that could set the stage for future contracts.

watchlist.title: Palantir's TITAN program extension
watchlist.body: Palantir's $480 million extension on the TITAN ground station program suggests a strong pipeline for defense contracts, making it one to watch.

watchlist.title: Sierra Space's Dream Chaser variant
watchlist.body: Having passed its critical design review, the Dream Chaser DoD variant's next steps will be crucial in determining its market viability.

watchlist.title: Anduril and L3Harris collaboration
watchlist.body: Their joint bid for a tactical SDA constellation could signal a shift in how defense contractors approach collaboration in space.

talent.statLabel: Job orders YoY · plus 2 starters per head, an 8-year first
talent.head: Demand has doubled. So has our hit rate.
talent.body: EVONA's job orders are up 2.0× year-over-year, and for the first time in our eight-year history we're placing two new starters per EVONA staff member. The first number says demand is real. The second says we're converting it, which in recruitment is the only number that actually matters. Growth is heaviest in Series B/C startups; primes are running flat. Compensation isn't the variable. The constraint is schedule risk in the primes: senior engineers leave Boeing, Lockheed, Northrop because they want to ship hardware before retirement.
